findings.summary: The falsifiable year-one success definition was replaced by a hedged list.

evidence.baseline: What success looks like at the end of that year is specific and falsifiable, and we state it so that we may be measured against it: fifteen to twenty-five committed mentors under signed agreement; ten completed mentor matches with documented outcomes (real people, real connections, real change); ... and the dataset that demonstrates, or fails to demonstrate, that the measurement of presence is real. We would rather discover in year one that some part of this is wrong than build for a decade on an assumption we never tested.
evidence.shipped: The proposed first-year evidence is more useful than a promise of scale: 1. Fifteen to twenty-five mentors or practitioners with clear agreements. ... 6. A dataset capable of weakening as well as supporting the measurement hypothesis.

findings.diagnosis: The baseline binds the builders to be measured against the definition; the shipped list proposes evidence without the binding. The committing frame (so that we may be measured against it, we would rather discover in year one that some part of this is wrong) is exactly what makes the figures honest, and it was the deleted half. The numbered list also fragments an argument prose was carrying, catalog 4.29's defect limb. Restored as prose; the outcomes fence became parentheses.

findings.summary: The founders-of-a-commons offer and the fundraise-as-values close were deleted entire.

evidence.baseline: The people who fund the early infrastructure of a new coordination system are not investors in a company. They are, in the older and truer sense, founders of a commons. ... We ask it because the alternative (the continuation of the coordination failure this volume has named) is not a passive default. It is an active choice, made by omission, every day the attempt is not made.
evidence.shipped: Founding partners should receive transparency and bounded governance appropriate to their role, not privileged access to participant data or permanent control over the commons. Money can fund proof. It cannot purchase the result.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression; the shipped bound preserved under R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT recording.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline offers founding partners full access to what we are learning and genuine participation in the governance of the work; the shipped pass replaced the offer with its safeguard. The safeguard is real (privileged data access and permanent control are the exact capture vectors chapter thirteen designs against) and is preserved here with Money can fund proof. It cannot purchase the result, which is the best sentence the shipped section had. Not kept in prose because it negates the restored offer; the tension is flagged, not reconciled.

findings.summary: The shipped budget-realism critique is preserved as drafting toward CTD-0009's paydown.

evidence.baseline: It funds a small core team at below-market pay with meaningful equity.
evidence.shipped: Those figures are planning hypotheses. Before they can support a funding case, they need a bottom-up budget with compensation, benefits, research costs, insurance, legal work, security, devices, participant payment, accessibility, contingency, and runway. "Below-market pay with meaningful equity" is not automatically responsible in a public-benefit project. The plan should show who bears the discount and whether they can afford it. ... Comparison with the cost of the internet proves nothing about what Providence needs.
evidence.shippedNote: Quoted at length because CTD-0009's paydown criteria require exactly this bottom-up model and this record is where the drafting survives.

findings.diagnosis: This finding runs the other way. The who-bears-the-discount question and the internet-comparison refusal are genuine analytical work the baseline lacks. They are preserved here rather than kept in prose because the baseline's claims (extraordinarily modest, economics are sound, the internet cost trillions) are the section's argument, and cutting them is a doctrine change the standing instruction reserves for the author.
